reviews.text: Fantastic forest/beach access campground. Great restrooms with hot showers. It's our favorite camp spot!

reviews.author: Clayton's R.
reviews.text: So this was the first time we've camped here since they reopened the park after extensive repair work. And I must say so happy to be back. Upgraded utilities, repaved most areas, and trimmed some bad trees out. Feels great, love this park, definitely recommend staying!

reviews.author: Jimmie F.
reviews.text: Big parking lot! Easy access to beach. Trail could use improving. But great stop!

reviews.author: Elizabeth N.
reviews.text: Had an amazing time this summer for the weekend. The camp sites were as expected and more. The trees and plants were beyond my expectations.  Friendly neighbor’s, lots of kiddos, Clean and hot showers. My Kiddos had a great time exploring, we went to the cookout area and gazed at the stars at night. Our favorite beach is 10minutes away. We were right between Lincoln city and Newport, right off the freeway! So tons of restaurants and grocery store near by!

reviews.author: Carlie D.
reviews.text:
Love it here. For such a large campground a lot of the sites made you feel secluded. We came in week of spring break for a few days and then a few days after spring break and let me tell you that place was empty after school started again.
Restrooms and showers were very clean, sites clean, playground super clean. Beach access is near the A “loop if I’m not mistaken and is super easy to get to with restrooms right before the beach(helpful with kiddos).  The check in office is only open from 4-6 and you need to check in but if your checking in late and know it call them to let them know they’re all so kind. Will definitely be coming back knowing there’s a little walking trail by the creek that’s behind some of the sites.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor用户（Tampa, FL·页面未署名）
reviews.text: This is a very popular campground, and we see why. First, location! It is 15 min away from many sightseeing spots that are sought after. Newport docks, the aquarium, Agate beach and Depoe Bay to name a few hot spots that are 10-15 min drive away... It's easy to access, right off of 101. Welcome was warm and friendly, helped guide us to our site. The beach access is a nice walk, minute to 7 minutes depending on your site. Bathrooms are all within a couple min from your site as well. Second, it is clean and well maintained. The grounds are immaculate. There are hosts for each loop and they cruise around keeping it clean and tidy... The showers and restrooms are what they are for how long this campground has been running. There is no laundry on site, something to keep in mind when staying here. Final part is long because we booked last minute, beyond grateful there was room to accommodate our 31 foot Class C RV, preferring full hookups. We were able to get a few sites last minute booking, and enjoyed staying at the different loops. WiFi works best closer to the beach. Site E 4 was pleasant. Shaded, as it seems most sites are... 3 min walk to beach. Site B11. Our fav! It was right up front, closest to the beach access... We didn't hear much traffic from 101... Site G 32. Shaded, quiet, 7 min walk to the beach, couple min to multiple restrooms. Seemed more private than our last two sites, bushes surrounding us. Walking path behind this site, access near the kids playground. We found the path behind us had a nice "fishing spot"... All in all, a lovely stay! A mix of tent and rv campers living our best summer. Many kids on bikes, pups on leashes, everyone enjoying the space and the beach. Fly a kite. Stroll the beach. Soak up the calm vibes of Beverly Beach State Park. We will be back :)
reviews.title: This is a very popular campground, and we see why

reviews.author: TripAdvisor用户（页面未署名）
reviews.text: BEAUTIFUL scenery-- lush, subtropical forest w/hiking trails throughout, and also around Spencer Creek. Pros: Clean and well-maintained, with nice showers, flush toilets and electrical hookups. Easy access to beach if in the "A" spots (close to highway, but little traffic noise)... A great coco-mat trail going down the sand hill to the beach made for easy access... Beach is LONG, so easy to find a quiet spot away from the crowds by the tunnel. Lots of fun kite-flying, building sand castles and looking for fossils. Dogs can be off-leash, but most weren't. Nice little store sold firewood and ice... Very close to Devil's Punchbowl... Short drives to Yaquina lighthouse and Cobble Beach tidepools, Depoe Bay (lots of whales!), Newport and Seal Rock (lots of shells; great beach!) Cons: Small campsites, very close together, so don't expect much privacy. We chose a bigger group site which was much roomier. Vigilant rangers/camp hosts drove by frequently. While we appreciated their presence, they could've done a better job with the noisemakers. There was a large, rowdy group near us who whooped and played loud music until almost 2:00 a.m. three of the four nights we were there. One ranger said they did a 10 p.m. noise patrol, but no evidence of that. It was 4th of July weekend so we expected some fireworks, but not booming M-80s from both the beach and within the campground. Where were the rangers then?

reviews.text: Stayed in a tent site here recently and it was just about perfect for our little family. It was quiet and fairly isolated, with a nice big flat spot near the fire pit for our tent. There was a ton of wildlife around too, as there were several huge Bluejays behind our site. We also spotted gray whales just offshore and spent most of one entire day hanging out on the beach. It was nice and expansive and we were able to find a good spot with no one around. Showers were great and the staff was super helpful/friendly. One of our new favorite spots to camp!

reviews.author: TripAdvisor用户（页面未署名）
reviews.text: We stayed in a Yurt in the F loop for a long weekend, which is the way to go for comfort. The yurt had 3 beds, a table and chairs and a much needed heater at night... We checked in online a few days prior to arrival, which allowed us to avoid the need to stop by the main desk for checkin. Beverly Beach is just a few miles north of Newport on Hwy 101, so it was convenient to run into town for lunch or dinner, or check out some of the sites. We ate dinner at the Chowder House one night, which I recommend. Back at the park, you follow the road to the beach and enter under the freeway overpass. A small stream divides the beach. I recommend staying to the right as you enter (facing the ocean)... Accessing the northern section of the beach gives you access to about a mile and a half of wide open sand. The furthest point you can reach ends at some interesting caves you can reach at low tide. The southern end of the beach is nice also, but turns rocky fairly quickly.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor用户（页面未署名）
reviews.text: This place was the best place we stayed for our RV trip. We were only able to stay one night, but it was well worth it for $54! It was all paved roads throughout the camping area and easy to get around with a 32' RV. They have one-night RV stalls just for people passing through or people like us who were just on a round trip tour. Our location was C5 and was located directly under a giant tree. It had a fire pit/BBQ and a picnic table as well as a large area behind the paved section where our RV was parked. We had full hookups, access to fire wood, a trail around the creek through the woods the grounds are located on, a convenience store at the top of the hill, and access to one of the largest areas of the beach without having to cross highway 101 (there was an access route under the bridge...). This is a place I would loved to spend an entire summer at if I had the ability to.

reviews.author: travelhwy101（Crescent City, California）
reviews.text: Beverly Beach - there is nowhere better. Anytime I need a trip to the Newport area, Beverly is my first stop. The bridge, the beach, the creek, the campsite. One of my absolute favorite places along the Oregon Coast. If you're camping, the showers are great, the camping spaces are secluded, and the stars are truly gorgeous. The walk down to the beach is quick, going under the Hwy 101 bridge, and straight onto white sand. I've viewed many a sunset here, and I'll never get bored of them! You can buy firewood when you're there, and I would highly recommend spending the night! Solo camp trips here are the best.
